chunks: And he narrated from Rashiq, the owner of Madarai, who said:

Al-Mu'addad sent for us while we were three men, and ordered each of us to mount a horse, to leave the third behind, and to go out in disguise, carrying nothing with us except a prayer mat on the saddle. He said to us: 'Go to Samarra.' He described a neighborhood and a house to us and said: 'When you arrive at it, you will find a black servant at the door; besiege the house, and whoever you see in it, bring me his head.'

We arrived in Samarra and found the matter as he had described. In the vestibule was a black servant weaving a mat in his hand. We asked him about the house and who was in it, and he said: 'Its owner.' By Allah, he did not turn to us nor did his heart feel anxious about us. We entered the house as we were ordered, and found a private house. Opposite the house was a curtain that I had never seen anything finer than, as if hands had just raised it at that moment. There was no one in the house.

We lifted the curtain and found a large room, as if a sea of water was in it. At the far end of the room was a mat, which we knew was floating on the water. Upon it stood a man, the most handsome of people in appearance, praying. He did not turn to us nor to any of our belongings.

Ahmad ibn Abdullah rushed forward to cross into the room, but he drowned in the water. He continued struggling until I stretched my hand to him, rescued him, brought him out, and he fell unconscious for a while. Then my second companion did the same action, and he suffered the same fate, while I remained stunned.

I said to the owner of the house: 'My excuse is with Allah and with you. By Allah, I do not know what the matter is, nor to whom I have come, and I am repentant to Allah.' He did not turn to anything we said, nor did he cease from what he was doing, which filled us with awe. We turned away from him.

Al-Mu'addad was waiting for us, and he had instructed the doorkeepers that as soon as we arrived, we should enter his presence at any time. We arrived at him during the night, and he had us brought in. He asked us about the news, so we narrated to him what we had seen. He said: 'Woe to you! Did anyone meet you before me, or did any cause or word pass between you and anyone else?' We said: 'No.' He said: 'I am not the grandson of my grandfather.' He swore with his strongest oath that if this news reached him, he would surely strike our necks. So we did not dare to report it until after his death.

key_terms.تكّة: A small mat or rug being woven
key_terms.كسب الدار: To enter or besiege the house
key_terms.نفي من جدي: A phrase of surprise or emphasis (literally: I am not the grandson of my grandfather)

ai.seo_question: What happened when Al-Mu'addad's men tried to capture the hidden figure in Samarra?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* illustrates the concept of *ghaybat al-qasira* (minor occultation) by depicting the Imam’s miraculous preservation from the Abbasid Caliph Al-Mu’addad, who feared the Imam’s presence would lead to his execution. The Imam’s deep absorption in prayer (*ghafla* over the observers) and the floating mat symbolize his divine protection and unique spiritual status, reinforcing the Shia belief in the Imam’s hidden yet active role during the period of concealment.
